mu_name_from: MuMain's _enum.h: MONSTER_SKELETON_WARRIOR = 14. mu.db's monster_kinds agrees at number 14, level 19, 525 health, and OpenMU's Version075 Lorencia.cs names it 'Skeleton Warrior' at that number and puts fifteen of them in the box at 95-175, 168-244.
note: Not a monster model. MU has no Monster##.bmd for the Skeleton Warrior: CreateMonster's case for MONSTER_SKELETON_WARRIOR - shared with the Death King and the Death Bone, which are other maps' - calls CreateCharacter(Key, MODEL_PLAYER, ...), sets c->Object.SubType = MODEL_SKELETON1, and for Type == 14 sets Scale 0.95, Weapon[0] = MODEL_GLADIUS and Weapon[1] = MODEL_BUCKLER. He is a player in a skeleton body holding a sword and a shield, which is why this file is a character - kind, parts, hands - with a monster block on it, and why the crowd stands him on the player's rig and not on a monster's.
parts_from: The one part is Skill/Skeleton01.bmd, which RenderCharacter draws whole in place of the five body parts: `else if (o->Type == MODEL_PLAYER && (o->SubType >= MODEL_SKELETON1 && o->SubType <= MODEL_SKELETON3)) RenderPartObject(&c->Object, o->SubType, ...)`. No helm, no armour, no gloves, no boots and no head - the body-part slots are never set for him, and the render branch does not read them. See Skeleton01.json for the part itself.
hands_from:
MODEL_GLADIUS is MODEL_SWORD + 6, so Item/Sword07.bmd; MODEL_BUCKLER is MODEL_SHIELD + 4, so Item/Shield05.bmd. Both already built. Held on the player rig's own grip bones - knife_gdf and hand_bofdgne01 - because that is the rig he is on; a monster names its own link bones and a character does not need to. See DarkKnight.json's hands_note.

The swing is picked the way a player's is, and the shield has a say in it. SetPlayerAttack's sword-group branch tests `Weapon[1].Type >= MODEL_SWORD && < MODEL_MACE + MAX_ITEM_INDEX` to decide between the four-way dual-wield cycle and the plain `PLAYER_ATTACK_SWORD_RIGHT1 + SwordCount % 2`; a Buckler is in the shield group, so he alternates Attack sword right 1 and 2 - actions 39 and 40 - and never the left-hand pair. Crowd.Moves.Armed reads the same ladder.
monster_from: scale 0.95 is CreateMonster's, in the `if (Type == 14)` half of the shared case, and it scales the whole figure including what he holds - a monster's weapon is drawn at the monster's Scale. model_index is -1 because there is no model to index: the play speeds are the player's table, from assets/players/rig/actions.json, which is what the shared actions library was built against. Nothing in assets/monsters/actions.json applies to him.
stance_from: SetPlayerStop, ZzzCharacter.cpp: a monster is never in a safe zone, Weapon[0] is in the sword group and the Gladius is not TwoHand, so PLAYER_STOP_SWORD - action 4 - and its walk, PLAYER_WALK_SWORD at 17. The same rows Clips.StanceActions gives any character holding a one-handed sword; Sword07.json declares the stance and this repeats it only because a monster entry has no weapon row to read it off.
sounds_from:
Not a monster's five slots. He is MODEL_PLAYER, whose Sounds[] are empty, and the client tests the sub-type in four places instead:

- walking, on rand_fps_check(16), the same roll as a monster's wandering noise: `if (SubType in SKELETON1..3) PlayBuffer(SOUND_BONE1, o)` - mBone1.wav, a rattle.
- the first key of an attack: `PlayBuffer(SOUND_BRANDISH_SWORD01 + rand() % 2, o)` - eSwingWeapon1 and eSwingWeapon2, the same pair a player's sword swings with.
- the first key of the shock: SOUND_BONE1 again.
- the death, above: SOUND_BONE2 - mBone2.wav, the pile landing.

Written into sounds.json as skeletonwarrior_move, skeletonwarrior_attack, skeletonwarrior_shock and skeletonwarrior_die, which is what Crowd.Named makes of 'Skeleton Warrior', so the crowd's ordinary monster events reach the right files without a special case.
not_built_note: Two lines in the client are about skeletons in Lorencia and are not this monster. `if (o->Kind == KIND_NPC && WorldActive == WD_0LORENCIA && Type == MODEL_PLAYER && SubType in SKELETON1..3)` turns an NPC skeleton to face 90 degrees and draws it lit by c->Level - that is the Halloween event's skeleton NPC standing in town, KIND_NPC, and the Warrior is KIND_MONSTER. And `c->Blood = true` in the shared case is read by nothing in 0.75's hit code that this project reaches; the blood the crowd throws on a landed blow is the client's ordinary `tc->Hit >= 1` and applies to him as to everything.
